title: Trump Allies Plan Insurrection Act Use Against Civil Demonstrations
description_medium: In November 2023, The Washington Post reported that Donald Trump and his allies were planning actions for a possible second term. Associates were drafting plans to invoke the Insurrection Act on the first day in office to deploy the military against civil demonstrations. The report described a proposal under discussion, not an order Trump had issued.
description_long: In November 2023, The Washington Post reported that Donald Trump and allies were mapping out how to use federal power if he won a second term. One part of the planning involved Project 2025, a partnership of conservative groups that was drafting proposed executive orders. People involved in those discussions and internal communications reviewed by the Post indicated that the plans contemplated invoking the Insurrection Act on the president’s first day to permit domestic military deployments against civil demonstrations. The report also said Trump had expressed regret about not using greater federal force during unrest in 2020 and had said he would not hesitate to do so in the future. These facts describe planning and rhetoric, not a decision to invoke the statute or a completed deployment. The Insurrection Act permits domestic military use in specified circumstances, and the prospect of using it against demonstrations raised constitutional and civil-liberties concerns. Trump’s campaign did not address the specific plans in response to the Post’s questions. The distinction between his own comments and plans drafted by associates is central to accurately describing the report.

corrected_wording.label: Correction to earlier proposal
corrected_wording.text: This replaces the earlier partial draft. The 2023 report supports plans drafted by Trump allies and associates to potentially invoke the Insurrection Act against civil demonstrations; it does not show that Trump personally made repeated promises to invoke it against Americans.

source_access_notes: Same-event Washington Post report retrieved and read. The assigned New York Times link covers January 6, 2021 and is unrelated to the 2023 planning report.
rationale: Replaces the unverified repeated personal promise with the specific 2023 planning account, attributes the Insurrection Act proposal to associates and Project 2025, and distinguishes plans from an executed order.
